<description>
**Problem:** On Arch Linux the installed `bitcoin` command doesn't work: `bitcoin -m node`, `bitcoin chainstate`, and similar commands all fail with `execvp failed to execute ... No such file or directory` (#35785). Arch installs the programs the wrapper runs into a different directory than the wrapper looks in.

**Solution:** Make the wrapper look for those programs in the directory they were actually installed to, rather than a hardcoded one. Small change to the wrapper (`src/bitcoin.cpp`), plus build-system changes to pass it the configured install directories, and a functional test for the installed layout. Details are in the commit messages.

Fixes #35785. Built from earlier PRs #36037, #35789, and #36085.
</description>

[2026-11-13] rc:4565541648 inline on src/bitcoin.cpp by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-11-13):
re: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36106#pullrequestreview-5876277519

In commit "build: respect CMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR/LIBEXECDIR in bitcoin wrapper" (7d5cab41d863d31f49e3a3d6dc661fbb975d7be9)

[quoted text omitted]
Thanks for testing this. It is a regression from this PR. The Nix cmake setup hook passes absolute values (`-DCMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR=$out/bin`, `-DCMAKE_INSTALL_LIBEXECDIR=$out/libexec`), and this line compares the wrapper's directory name with the whole `BITCOIN_BINDIR` value, so `"bin" == "/tmp/inst/bin"` is false and the libexec lookup is skipped. The wrapper then only tries `bin/bitcoin-node`, which is the path in the error. On master the hardcoded `bin` and `libexec` names happen to match the Nix layout, so it works there. The functional test didn't catch this because it skips absolute values.

This is the limitation you pointed out in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36106#discussion_r3904899287, and documenting it wasn't enough. The latest push fixes it by having CMake compute the bindir name and the path from the bindir to the libexecdir from `CMAKE_INSTALL_FULL_BINDIR` and `CMAKE_INSTALL_FULL_LIBEXECDIR`, so the wrapper looks in `../libexec` (or `../lib` on Arch) whether the configured values are relative or absolute. The test now uses the absolute values too, instead of skipping them.
